data.narrative:
Monumental is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $32M to date. The peer universe comprises three same-stage, same-sector private comparables (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity) alongside a broader frontier-tech comp set of eight private firms and one public proxy.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $32M total raised and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage step-ups, implies $61M. Peer-median valuation using the three robotics-stage-matched comparables yields $1.8B, with the range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B. The peer-median method carries greater weight given the direct sector and stage alignment of the sample.

The triangulated analysis produces a wide range: $52M (low), $905M (median), and $2.0B (high). The material spread reflects tension between the stage-progression method—which relies on raised capital as a proxy absent operating metrics—and the peer set, where recent private robotics valuations have commanded substantial premiums. Key uncertainties include revenue traction relative to peer performance, capital efficiency, and market timing within the current frontier-tech funding environment. Resolution of these factors would narrow the range materially, particularly in distinguishing whether Monumental tracks closer to the lower-bound stage progression or the peer-derived valuation band.
